label: Luke 3:1
text: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

label: Luke 3:2
text: in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.

label: Luke 3:3
text: He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.

label: Luke 3:4
text: As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.

label: Luke 3:5
text: Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.

label: Luke 3:6
text: All flesh will see God’s salvation.’”

label: Luke 3:7
text: He said therefore to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

label: Luke 3:8
text: Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and don’t begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father;’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones!

variants.note: Also A, C, D, W, Theta, 33, 565, 700, 1424 and the Byzantine text, which the WEB follows; the reading of the WEB (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 3:8).

variants.reading: και μη δοξητε λεγειν εν εαυτοις ('And do not think to say to yourselves')
variants.note: Read by Codex Regius and others (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 3:8); no manuscript node for these witnesses exists in this graph.

label: Luke 3:9
text: Even now the ax also lies at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.”

label: Luke 3:10
text: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?”

label: Luke 3:11
text: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”

label: Luke 3:12
text: Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what must we do?”

label: Luke 3:13
text: He said to them, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”

label: Luke 3:14
text: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”

label: Luke 3:15
text: As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,

label: Luke 3:16
text: John answered them all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,

label: Luke 3:17
text: whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”

label: Luke 3:18
text: Then with many other exhortations he preached good news to the people,

label: Luke 3:19
text: but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,

label: Luke 3:20
text: added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.

label: Luke 3:21
text: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also had been baptized, and was praying. The sky was opened,

label: Luke 3:22
text: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice came out of the sky, saying “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”

label: Luke 3:23
text: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

label: Luke 3:24
text: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,

label: Luke 3:25
text: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,

label: Luke 3:26
text: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,

label: Luke 3:27
text: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,

label: Luke 3:28
text: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er,

label: Luke 3:29
text: the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,

label: Luke 3:30
text: the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,

label: Luke 3:31
text: the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,

label: Luke 3:32
text: the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,

label: Luke 3:33
text: the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,

label: Luke 3:34
text: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,

label: Luke 3:35
text: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,

label: Luke 3:36
text: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,

label: Luke 3:37
text: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,

label: Luke 3:38
text: the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.

label: John's ministry began in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar
statement: John's public appearance is dated to the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar - AD 28/29 counting from Tiberius's accession on Augustus's death in AD 14, or AD 26/27 on William Ramsay's counting from Tiberius's co-princeps association in AD 12.

label: Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
statement: Pontius Pilate held the governorship (prefecture) of Judea at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

label: Herod Antipas was tetrarch of Galilee in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
statement: Herod (Antipas) was tetrarch of Galilee at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

label: Herod Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
statement: Philip, Antipas's brother, was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis at the time Luke dates; Josephus lists his territories as Gaulanitis, Trachonitis, Paneas, Batanea, Auranitis and part of the House of Zenodorus, without naming Ituraea.

label: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene
statement: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene (the region of Abila, northwest of Damascus) at the time Luke dates; whether he is the Lysanias executed by Antony in 36 BCE, a younger tetrarch of the reduced Abilene, or the inscription's Tiberian-era tetrarch is debated.

label: Annas shared the high-priesthood formula with Caiaphas
statement: Luke names the high priesthood of 'Annas and Caiaphas' jointly; Annas (Ananus son of Seth) had been high priest AD 6-15 and remained the dominant figure of the priestly house while Caiaphas, his son-in-law's appointee line, held the office, though a joint high priesthood was not permitted under Jewish law.

label: Caiaphas was high priest in the fifteenth year of Tiberius
statement: Joseph Caiaphas held the high priesthood at the time Luke dates: the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar.

label: Luke applies Isaiah 40:3-5 to John, quoting the fuller text through 'all flesh shall see God's salvation'
statement: Luke introduces John's preaching with Isaiah 40:3-5 from 'the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet', quoting the fuller passage whose closing ('All flesh will see God's salvation') Matthew's quotation of Isaiah 40:3 does not carry.

label: John warned the crowds coming for baptism to flee the wrath to come and produce fruits worthy of repentance
statement: John said to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him: 'You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance.'

label: John warned against relying on descent from Abraham: God can raise up children to Abraham from stones
statement: John told the crowds not to say 'We have Abraham for our father', for God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

label: John told the crowds that he who has two coats or food should share with those who have none
statement: To the multitudes asking what they must do, John answered: 'He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.'

label: Tax collectors came to John's baptism and were told to collect no more than what was appointed
statement: Tax collectors came to be baptized and asked John what to do; he told them, 'Collect no more than that which is appointed to you' - presupposing tax collectors with fixed assessments in the Jordan region.

label: Soldiers asked John what to do and were told not to extort by violence and to be content with their wages
statement: Soldiers asked John what they must do; he told them to extort no one by violence, accuse no one wrongfully, and be content with their wages - presupposing soldiers serving in the region.

label: The people were in expectation and wondered whether John might be the Christ
statement: As the people were in expectation and all reasoned in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he was the Christ, John answered them all that one mightier than he was coming.

label: John preached that the mightier one would baptize with the Holy Spirit and with fire
statement: John answered the people that he baptized with water, but the mightier one whose sandal strap he was not worthy to loosen would baptize them in the Holy Spirit and fire.

label: John described the coming one with a winnowing fan: wheat gathered into the barn, chaff burned with unquenchable fire
statement: John's image of the coming judge: 'whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.'

label: Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his work
statement: Jesus himself, when he began (to teach), was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph.

label: Luke's genealogy traces Jesus (as was supposed, through Joseph) from Heli back through David's son Nathan to Adam and God
statement: Luke's genealogy runs Joseph - Heli ... Nathan - David ... Abraham - ... - Adam - God: through Nathan, not Solomon; the names from David to Jesus differ entirely from Matthew's list; Luke reaches back to Adam, Matthew only to Abraham.

label: Lysanias
dates: early first century CE (Luke); a Lysanias executed by Antony died 36 BCE (Josephus)

label: Annas
aka: Ananus son of Seth; high priest AD 6-15
dates: high priest AD 6-15; flourished to c. 40 CE

Nahum, father of Esli (Luke 3:25; not the prophet)
Neri, father of Shealtiel in Luke's list (Luke 3:27; Matthew gives Jeconiah)
Matthat, son of Levi (Luke 3:29; a second Matthat son of Levi in the list)
Levi, son of Simeon (Luke 3:29; a second Levi in the list)

Nathan, son of David (Luke 3:31; Matthew traces David through Solomon)
Aram, son of Hezron (Luke 3:33; Matthew 1:4 calls him Ram)
Cainan, son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36; the LXX name between Arphaxad and Shelah, absent from the Hebrew Genesis)
Lamech, son of Methuselah (Luke 3:36; not the Lamech of Cain's line)
Cainan, son of Mahalaleel (Luke 3:37; a second Cainan in the list)

label: Wikipedia: Threshing floor (winnowing fork or fan; chaff blown away, grain falls at the winnower's feet)
title: Threshing floor
excerpt: the broken stalks and grain were collected and then thrown up into the air with a wooden winnowing fork or a winnowing fan. The chaff would be blown away by the wind; the short torn straw would fall some distance away; while the heavier grain would fall at the winnower's feet.
